Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Real, confirmed production bug found earlier tonight: the Minecraft server image is hardcoded to a single Java version, but different Minecraft versions require different Java runtimes — any customer picking an incompatible combination gets a permanent crash loop with zero clear error surfaced anywhere in the platform. The owner has explicitly approved both the immediate customer fix and the platform-wide fix below.

## Confirmed root cause (from a live investigation tonight)
- `worker/game-config.ts`'s `MINECRAFT_IMAGE` constant is hardcoded to `itzg/minecraft-server:java21` for every Minecraft server regardless of chosen version.
- `lib/game-config.ts`'s `MINECRAFT_RELEASE_VERSIONS` offers versions including `26.2/26.1.2/26.1.1/26.1`, which per Mojang's own real requirement need Java 25+, not Java 21.
- A customer (yu chen, server `minecraft-qj4rxt`, VMID 132, node-4, guest `10.20.3.103`) picked `26.2` and has been crash-looping every ~15 seconds since creation: `docker logs mc` shows `Minecraft 26.1 and newer requires running the server with Java 25 or above.` — confirmed live, container never actually started.
- Every existing platform health check (`GAME_UPDATE`, `GAME_POWER start/restart`) only verifies the container/systemd service OBJECT exists, not that the actual game process bound the port — which is why this went undetected. A live external connection test to the real public port got "connection refused" right now.

## Task 1 — Fix yu chen's server (approved, do this for real)
Bump this server's image to a real Java-25-capable tag and recreate the container so his server actually comes up on version 26.2 (the owner wants him to keep his chosen version, not be downgraded). Use `itzg/minecraft-server`'s real published tags — check Docker Hub / their GitHub for the actual correct tag name for Java 25 support (don't guess a tag name that might not exist; their tagging convention has historically been things like `java21`, `java17`, etc. — find the real current equivalent for Java 25, which may be `java25` or may require a specific version tag if that's not GA as a named tag yet — verify before using). Apply this as the SAME code path task 2 builds below (i.e., build the real fix first, then use it to actually recreate this customer's container), not as a separate one-off hack.

## Task 2 — Fix this platform-wide, "plug and play" for every future provision and every future version change
The owner wants this to "just work flawlessly" regardless of which version a customer selects, now and going forward — no more hardcoded single image.

1. **Research the REAL Java-version requirement per Minecraft version** — don't guess a mapping. Check Mojang's own official documentation/release notes for which Minecraft versions require which minimum Java version (there have been several real cutover points historically — e.g. 1.17+ needed Java 16, 1.18+ needed Java 17, and now 26.1+ needs Java 25 per the confirmed error above). Also check `itzg/minecraft-server`'s own documentation for whether their image can auto-detect/auto-select the right Java version internally (some versions of that image bundle multiple JDKs and select automatically based on the requested `VERSION` env var — if that's true for the current stable/full image tag, the REAL fix might be as simple as switching to that auto-detecting image tag instead of a version-pinned one like `java21`, which would be the cleanest, most "plug and play" fix and worth strongly preferring over a hand-maintained mapping table if it's real and works).
2. **Implement the fix** in `worker/game-config.ts`/`lib/game-config.ts` (read both in full, and anywhere else `MINECRAFT_IMAGE` or version-to-image logic is referenced — grep for all usages first) so that:
   - New provisions automatically get a working image/Java combination for whatever version the customer picked at signup, with zero manual intervention.
   - A customer changing their Minecraft version later (via the existing version-config UI) also gets a compatible image recreated automatically — check how version changes currently flow (likely the same `gameserver.config` action seen in tonight's investigation) and make sure this new logic applies there too, not just at initial provision.
   - Existing servers on older, already-working versions/images are NOT disrupted — this must be additive/corrective, not a blanket image bump that could break currently-fine java21 servers on older MC versions.
3. **Add a real health check improvement** so this class of bug (container object exists but game process never actually bound the port) gets caught automatically in the future — check `worker/game-config.ts`'s or wherever `GAME_UPDATE`/health-verification logic lives, and add a real "is the game port actually listening / did the process log a successful startup line" check rather than just "does the container/service exist." This is what would have caught this bug immediately instead of it silently persisting for hours.
4. **Consider the version picker itself**: if some versions genuinely can't be made to work reliably yet (e.g. brand-new releases the image maintainers haven't caught up on), it may be safer to not offer them in `MINECRAFT_RELEASE_VERSIONS` until confirmed working, rather than offering a version that's guaranteed to crash-loop. Use judgment — if your research from step 1 gives you a real, working fix for all 4 currently-offered new versions, keep them all offered; if any remain genuinely unresolvable, flag it rather than silently leaving a broken option in the picker.

## Process (mandatory) — this is a live, paying customer's server, be careful
- Read `worker/game-config.ts`, `lib/game-config.ts`, and `prisma/catalog.ts`'s Minecraft setup script in full before changing anything.
- DB reads only via `db` from `lib/db`, scripts under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` via `npx tsx`, deleted after. NEVER print/construct a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string.
- Test the real fix by actually recreating yu chen's container and verifying: (a) `docker logs` shows a clean real startup (not the Java-version error), (b) the game process actually shows in `ss -tlnp` as bound to the port, (c) a real external connection test to the public port succeeds (not connection-refused).
- Before recreating this customer's container, check current build/deploy state (`ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"`) — this task involves worker code, so once your code changes are ready, you'll need a real deploy for the WORKER service specifically (check how the worker gets deployed — likely part of the same `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` pipeline, restarting `nxeon-worker`) to pick up the new logic before you can use it to fix yu chen's server for real. If a build/deploy is already running from another concurrent agent, wait for it to clear, then run your own build+deploy for this fix (this is an exception to tonight's "commit-only, don't deploy" rule since you specifically need the new code live to actually fix a real customer's broken server — but check nothing else is mid-build first, and don't leave staging/production in a half-built state if anything goes wrong).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Commit and push to `main`.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` covering the real Java-version-to-Minecraft-version mapping/logic you implemented and why.

Report back: the real fix architecture (auto-detecting image vs. explicit mapping table, and why), confirmation yu chen's server is now actually reachable (real evidence: clean logs, port listening, successful external connection test), and confirmation this is genuinely "plug and play" for all future provisions and version changes without requiring any manual per-server intervention.

6	 * performs no I/O.

9	 * a player runs — Paper vs Vanilla, Carbon vs Oxide, …) and a versioned list of
10	 * *settings fields* that drive a dynamic UI. Fields are intentionally limited to
11	 * the handful of options players actually change, keyed on the game's own real
12	 * config keys (server.properties, PalWorldSettings.ini, cvars, …) — no invented
13	 * cvars — so a future real "apply" step can render them 1:1.

18	
19	/** Bump when the field set changes in a way the worker/apply step must notice. */
20	export const GAME_CONFIG_VERSION = 1;
21	
22	export type FieldType = "enum" | "bool" | "int" | "string";
23	
24	/**
25	 * When a setting takes effect:
26	 *  - "deploy": needs a server restart / redeploy (world seed, tickrate, …)
27	 *  - "live":   can be pushed to a running server (motd, pvp, max players, …)

138	export const RESTART_WAIT_SLEEP_S = 2;

140	/**
141	 * Should `gameUpdateSweep` even enqueue a check for this candidate?
142	 *
143	 * `Server.status` is the VM's own power state, not the game service inside
144	 * it — `gamePower`'s own doc comment (worker/game-control.ts) is explicit
145	 * that the two are "genuinely different things". So a customer who presses
146	 * Stop on the dashboard (GAME_POWER "stop") leaves `status` at RUNNING
147	 * forever, and the sweep — which only ever looks at `status`+`autoUpdate` —
148	 * kept enqueueing a GAME_UPDATE job against it every cycle with no way to
149	 * know the service was off on purpose. Every one of those jobs then failed
150	 * with "your game server is NOT running", which is TRUE and also not news:
151	 * the customer did that themselves.
152	 *
153	 * Found live 2026-09-17: suplosmp (bedrock) generated a FAILED GAME_UPDATE
154	 * job on every single sweep for 28+ straight hours after its owner pressed

156	 * ignore it" erosion `notifyFailureOnce` already exists to prevent for
157	 * notifications, just unaddressed on the job-creation side.
158	 *
159	 * `gamePower` persists the post-action `systemctl is-active` result to
160	 * `Server.gameConfig._serviceState` (its own doc comment explains why: the
161	 * dashboard's status dot needed it). That is the one signal that distinguishes
162	 * "the customer turned this off" from "this crashed" — a crash is never
163	 * written here, only an explicit start/stop/restart action is. So only the
164	 * exact value "inactive" (a clean, completed stop) skips the sweep; anything
165	 * else — "failed" (a crash), "activating" (mid-restart), missing/stale — is
166	 * still checked normally, because those are precisely what this job exists
167	 * to catch.
168	 */
169	export function eligibleForUpdateSweep(gameConfig: unknown): boolean {
170	  const state = (gameConfig as Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined)?.["_serviceState"];
171	  return state !== "inactive";

174	/**
175	 * Build the remote script.
176	 *
177	 * Design rules, each of which the old one-liner broke:
178	 *
179	 *  - No `set -e` and no trailing `; true`. Control flow is explicit, and the exit
180	 *    status is irrelevant — the MARKERS are the contract, so a truncated or
181	 *    dropped connection is detectable (no `NXGU:END`) rather than indistinguishable
182	 *    from success.
183	 *  - steamcmd's own exit code is not trusted (it is famously unreliable and
184	 *    frequently non-zero on a perfectly good update). We match its own success
185	 *    line instead, and report the code alongside.
186	 *  - "no unit matched" is an outcome we emit, not a branch we swallow.
187	 *  - The post-restart state is polled and reported verbatim. `active` is the only
188	 *    thing that will be called success upstream.

190	 * `family` is constrained to GAME_FAMILIES by the caller AND re-checked here, so
191	 * nothing unvalidated is interpolated into the shell.
192	 */
193	export function updateCommand(family: GameFamily): string {
194	  if (!GAME_FAMILIES.includes(family)) throw new Error(`not a game family: ${family}`);
195	  const appId = STEAM_APPID[family];
196	  const svc = SERVICE_HINT[family];
197	  // Both are compile-time constants from the tables above — never customer input.
198	
199	  // Emitted by every branch that must not go on to restart the service.
200	  const stopHere = [
201	    `st=$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null)`,
202	    `say "SKIPPED_RESTART:1"`,
203	    `say "STATE:${"$"}{st:-unknown}"`,
204	    `say "END"`,
205	    `exit 0`,
206	  ];
207	
208	  const steam = appId
209	    ? [
210	        `fresh=0`,
211	        `if command -v steamcmd >/dev/null 2>&1; then`,
212	        `  out=$(steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update ${appId} validate +quit 2>&1); rc=$?`,
213	        `  say "STEAM_RC:$rc"`,
214	        // steamcmd prints "Success! App '<id>' already up to date." when there was
215	        // nothing to download, and "Success! App '<id>' fully installed." when
216	        // there was. Both used to match one grep, so the two outcomes were
217	        // indistinguishable — see the CURRENT/OK split in the header note.
218	        `  if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Success! App '${appId}' already up to date"; then`,
219	        `    say "STEAM:CURRENT"`,
220	        `  elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Success! App '${appId}'"; then`,
221	        `    fresh=1; say "STEAM:OK"`,
222	        `  else`,
223	        `    say "STEAM:FAIL"`,
224	        `    printf '%s' "$out" | grep -i 'error' | head -3 | while IFS= read -r l; do say "STEAM_ERR:$l"; done`,
225	        `  fi`,
226	        `else`,
227	        `  say "STEAM:ABSENT"`,
228	        `fi`,
229	        // Do NOT bounce a healthy game server for an update that did not happen:
230	        // a restart kicks every connected player off for nothing, and it would
231	        // make "the service was restarted" the only true half of a false claim.
232	        // This now also covers the "already up to date" case, which is the COMMON
233	        // one — it ran every 6 hours and disconnected everybody four times a day.
234	        `if [ "$fresh" != "1" ]; then`,
235	        ...stopHere.map((l) => `  ${l}`),
236	        `fi`,
237	      ].join("\n")
238	    : [
239	        // No update source exists for this family, so there is nothing a restart
240	        // could apply. Restarting anyway is a pure loss: every connected player
241	        // is disconnected, four times a day, forever, to change nothing. The
242	        // rule two paragraphs up applies here MOST, and used not to be applied
243	        // here at all.
244	        `say "STEAM:NA"`,
245	        ...stopHere,
246	      ].join("\n");
247	
248	  return [
249	    `say() { printf 'NXGU:%s\\n' "$1"; }`,
250	    // 1. Resolve the unit. `systemctl cat` succeeds only for a unit that exists.
251	    `unit=""`,
252	    `for c in ${svc} ${svc}-server; do`,
253	    `  if systemctl cat "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then unit="$c"; break; fi`,
254	    `done`,
255	    `if [ -z "$unit" ]; then`,
256	    `  unit=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --plain --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -i ${family} | head -1 | awk '{print $1}')`,
257	    `fi`,
258	    `if [ -z "$unit" ]; then say "UNIT:NONE"; say "END"; exit 0; fi`,
259	    `say "UNIT:$unit"`,
260	    `was=$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null); say "WAS:${"$"}{was:-unknown}"`,
261	    // 2. Update the game files, where such a thing exists.
262	    steam,
263	    // 3. Restart, and report the real result of the restart call.
264	    `systemctl restart "$unit" >/dev/null 2>&1; say "RESTART_RC:$?"`,
265	    // 4. Wait for it to settle. A game server can take a while to open its port,
266	    //    so "activating" is a distinct answer from "failed" and both are reported.
267	    `i=0; st=""`,
268	    `while [ $i -lt ${RESTART_WAIT_TRIES} ]; do`,
269	    `  st=$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null)`,
270	    `  if [ "$st" = "active" ] || [ "$st" = "failed" ]; then break; fi`,
271	    `  i=$((i+1)); sleep ${RESTART_WAIT_SLEEP_S}`,
272	    `done`,
273	    `say "STATE:${"$"}{st:-unknown}"`,
274	    `say "END"`,
275	  ].join("\n");
276	}

279	// Parsing

281	
282	export type GameUpdateFacts = {
283	  /** The systemd unit the script acted on, or null when nothing matched. */
284	  unit: string | null;
285	  /** `systemctl is-active` before the restart. */
286	  wasActive: string;
287	  /** Exit code of `systemctl restart`, or null when it never ran. */
288	  restartRc: number | null;
289	  /** `systemctl is-active` after the restart, settled or timed out. */
290	  state: string;
291	  /**
292	   * "ok" = steamcmd downloaded a NEW build. "current" = it confirmed the server
293	   * was already up to date and downloaded nothing. Collapsing those two into one
294	   * value is what made "<game> updated on <host>" fire every 6 hours forever.
295	   */
296	  steam: "ok" | "current" | "failed" | "absent" | "na" | "unknown";
297	  steamRc: number | null;
298	  steamErrors: string[];
299	  /** Did the script run to completion? No END marker means we know nothing. */
300	  complete: boolean;
301	};
302	
303	export function parseGameUpdateOutput(out: string): GameUpdateFacts {
304	  const text = String(out ?? "");
305	  const one = (re: RegExp): string | null => re.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
306	
307	  const steamRaw = one(/^NXGU:STEAM:(\w+)$/m);
308	  const steam =
309	    steamRaw === "OK" ? "ok"
310	    : steamRaw === "CURRENT" ? "current"
311	    : steamRaw === "FAIL" ? "failed"
312	    : steamRaw === "ABSENT" ? "absent"
313	    : steamRaw === "NA" ? "na"
314	    : "unknown";
315	
316	  const rc = (re: RegExp): number | null => {
317	    const v = one(re);
318	    return v === null ? null : Number(v);
319	  };
320	
321	  const unitLine = one(/^NXGU:UNIT:(.+)$/m);
322	  const steamErrors: string[] = [];
323	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/^NXGU:STEAM_ERR:(.*)$/gm)) steamErrors.push(m[1].trim());
324	
325	  return {
326	    unit: unitLine === null || unitLine === "NONE" ? null : unitLine.trim(),
327	    wasActive: one(/^NXGU:WAS:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
328	    restartRc: rc(/^NXGU:RESTART_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
329	    state: one(/^NXGU:STATE:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
330	    steam,
331	    steamRc: rc(/^NXGU:STEAM_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
332	    steamErrors,
333	    complete: /^NXGU:END$/m.test(text),
334	  };
335	}

337	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
338	// The verdict
339	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
340	
341	export type GameUpdateVerdict =
342	  | {
343	      ok: true;
344	      title: string;
345	      body: string;
346	      /**
347	       * Is this an EVENT worth interrupting the customer for?
348	       *
349	       * This runs unattended every 6 hours. `notifyFailureOnce` already exists
350	       * because "the customer would learn to ignore them — which is the same
351	       * outcome as not telling them"; the success path had no equivalent and
352	       * notified on every single pass, so a healthy server produced four
353	       * notifications a day, forever, all of them titled "<game> updated on
354	       * <host>" when nothing had been updated. Only a real, observed change is
355	       * an event.
356	       */
357	      notify: boolean;
358	    }
359	  | { ok: false; reason: string };
360	
361	/**
362	 * Turn observed facts into the one thing the customer is told.
363	 *
364	 * Every refusal names the reason AND the command to run, because "update failed"
365	 * on a game server six hours after the fact is useless without a next step.
366	 * Every success states precisely what was proven — including, for minecraft and
367	 * terraria, that no game update took place at all, because there is no update
368	 * source for those families and saying otherwise was the original lie.
369	 */
370	export function judgeGameUpdate(opts: {
371	  family: GameFamily;
372	  hostname: string;
373	  facts: GameUpdateFacts;
374	}): GameUpdateVerdict {
375	  const { family, hostname, facts: f } = opts;
376	  const appId = STEAM_APPID[family];
377	
378	  if (!f.complete) {
379	    return {
380	      ok: false,
381	      reason:
382	        `the update script did not run to completion on ${hostname} (no end marker), so nothing about ` +
383	        `this run can be verified — the connection may have dropped or the command timed out. ` +
384	        `Nothing is being claimed. Re-run it by hand: systemctl status <your ${family} unit>`,
385	    };
386	  }
387	
388	  if (!f.unit) {
389	    return {
390	      ok: false,
391	      reason:
392	        `no systemd service for ${family} was found on ${hostname}, so nothing was updated and ` +
393	        `nothing was restarted. Check what the server actually runs with: ` +
394	        `systemctl list-units --type=service | grep -i ${family}`,
395	    };
396	  }
397	
398	  if (appId && f.steam === "absent") {
399	    return {
400	      ok: false,
401	      reason:
402	        `steamcmd is not installed on ${hostname}, so the ${family} game files were NOT updated. ` +
403	        `Auto-update cannot work on this server until it is present: apt-get install -y steamcmd ` +
404	        `(or reinstall from the ${family} image).`,
405	    };
406	  }
407	
408	  if (appId && f.steam !== "ok" && f.steam !== "current") {
409	    const detail = f.steamErrors.length ? ` steamcmd said: ${f.steamErrors.slice(0, 3).join(" | ")}` : "";
410	    return {
411	      ok: false,
412	      reason:
413	        `steamcmd did not report a successful update of app ${appId} on ${hostname} ` +
414	        `(exit ${f.steamRc ?? "unknown"}), so the game files were not updated and the service was ` +
415	        `left alone.${detail} Re-run by hand: steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update ${appId} validate +quit`,
416	    };
417	  }
418	
419	  // Nothing was restarted on these paths, so the state we observed is simply the
420	  // state the server was already in — do not describe it as a restart outcome.
421	  const restarted = f.steam === "ok";
422	
423	  if (f.state !== "active") {
424	    return {
425	      ok: false,
426	      reason: restarted
427	        ? `${f.unit} on ${hostname} is "${f.state}" after the restart` +
428	          (f.restartRc !== null && f.restartRc !== 0 ? ` (systemctl restart exited ${f.restartRc})` : "") +
429	          `, so your game server is NOT running. It was "${f.wasActive}" before this ran. ` +
430	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`
431	        : `${f.unit} on ${hostname} is "${f.state}" — your game server is NOT running. Nothing was ` +
432	          `updated or restarted by this check, so this is not something we just did to it. ` +
433	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`,
434	    };
435	  }
436	
437	  if (f.steam === "ok") {
438	    return {
439	      ok: true,
440	      notify: true, // a new build really was downloaded and applied
441	      title: `${family} updated on ${hostname}`,
442	      body:
443	        `steamcmd downloaded a new build of app ${appId}, and ${f.unit} was restarted and is active again ` +
444	        `(verified with systemctl, not assumed from an exit code).`,
445	    };
446	  }
447	
448	  if (f.steam === "current") {
449	    return {
450	      ok: true,
451	      notify: false, // nothing happened; four of these a day is noise, not news
452	      title: `${family} on ${hostname} is already up to date`,
453	      body:
454	        `steamcmd confirmed app ${appId} is already up to date, so nothing was downloaded and ${f.unit} was ` +
455	        `NOT restarted — no players were disconnected. It is active.`,
456	    };
457	  }
458	
459	  // No update source exists for this family. Say that, rather than implying one —
460	  // and do not restart, which is all this job could otherwise do here.
461	  return {
462	    ok: true,
463	    notify: false,
464	    title: `${family} server checked on ${hostname}`,
465	    body:
466	      `${f.unit} is active (verified). ${family} has no automatic update source on Nxeon, so there was ` +
467	      `nothing to download and your server was NOT restarted — restarting it every few hours would ` +
468	      `disconnect your players to change nothing. Update the server files yourself when a new version ships.`,
469	  };
470	}

There is **no auto-detection or auto-selection feature** mentioned in the documentation. The image tags are static and must be manually specified. Users are responsible for selecting the appropriate Java version tag based on their Minecraft server type and version.

The documentation notes that the `latest` tag shifts with new Java versions but does not automatically detect the server's VERSION variable to select the correct Java runtime.

# Available Docker Image Tags

## Active Tags

**latest** & **stable**: Both track Java 25 on Ubuntu with HotSpot JVM across amd64, arm64, and riscv64 architectures. "Always tracks the most recent commit on the main branch" (latest) and "Always tracks the most recent release" (stable). Both are LTS-designated.

**java25**: Java 25 on Ubuntu with HotSpot, supporting amd64, arm64, and riscv64.

**java25-alpine**: Java 25 on Alpine Linux with HotSpot for amd64 and arm64.

**java25-graalvm**: Java 25 with GraalVM on Oracle distribution (amd64, arm64). *Deprecated.*

**java21**, **java21-alpine**, **java21-jdk**: Java 21 LTS variants on Ubuntu/Alpine with HotSpot. The -jdk variant explicitly includes JDK tools.

**java17**, **java17-alpine**, **java17-graalvm**: Java 17 LTS options on Ubuntu/Alpine/Oracle distributions.

**java16**, **java11**, **java8**: Legacy versions (java11 and java8 are LTS). Support varies; java8/11/16 include armv7 architecture support.

**java24**, **java24-graalvm**: Java 24 variants. *Deprecated.*

## Deprecated Tags

Numerous older tags (adopt13-15, java19-20, java23, openj9 variants) are marked deprecated.

**Note on auto-selection**: The "latest" and "stable" tags provide automatic Java version tracking without explicit version numbers.

name: CI

# Typecheck + unit tests on every push and every pull request. Nothing here
# touches Proxmox, Stripe, Mailcow, a database or the network beyond the npm
# registry: the whole suite is pure functions (test/*.test.ts).
on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:

# A newer push to the same ref cancels the older run.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  check:
    name: typecheck + tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      # `prisma generate` and `import "@prisma/client"` want the variable to
      # exist; nothing in CI ever connects. This is not a real host.
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://ci:ci@127.0.0.1:5432/ci?schema=public
      # Keep the suite honest about being offline/deterministic.
      CI: "true"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # The Prisma client is generated, not committed. Type-checking `lib/**`
      # (and importing lib/mailer.ts from the dunning test) needs the generated
      # model types, so this must run before tsc and before the tests. Generation
      # reads prisma/schema.prisma only — it never contacts a database.
      - name: Generate Prisma client
        run: npx prisma generate

      - name: Typecheck (tsc --noEmit)
        run: |
          # tsc currently reports TS5097 for every `import … from "../lib/x.ts"`
          # in test/*.test.ts: the tests import with an explicit .ts extension
          # (which the `tsx --test` runner requires) while the tsconfig does not
          # set `allowImportingTsExtensions`. Those lines are the established,
          # pre-existing exception in this repo — everything else must be clean.
          #
          # The filter is deliberately narrower than the `grep -v "test/.*test.ts"`
          # convention used by hand: it drops ONLY TS5097 lines from test files, so
          # a genuine type error in a test still fails this job.
          npx tsc --noEmit > tsc.log 2>&1 || true
          grep -vE '^test/[^ ]+\.test\.ts\([0-9]+,[0-9]+\): error TS5097:' tsc.log > tsc-unexpected.log || true

## 2026-09-20 — Minecraft: per-version Java runtime (was hardcoded to java21 for every version)

**Incident.** `worker/game-config.ts`'s `MINECRAFT_IMAGE` was a single hardcoded
`itzg/minecraft-server:java21` applied to every Minecraft server regardless of the customer's chosen
`VERSION`, and `prisma/catalog.ts`'s provisioning `setupScript` baked the identical literal image tag
in directly — only the `VERSION` env var itself was ever substituted per-customer
(`applyGameConfigEnv`), never the image. Minecraft 26.1 and newer (offered in
`MINECRAFT_RELEASE_VERSIONS`) requires Java 25; Java 21 refuses to even start it. Found live via a
real customer server (`minecraft-qj4rxt`, picked 26.2): `docker logs mc` showed "Minecraft 26.1 and
newer requires running the server with Java 25 or above." on a permanent ~15s crash loop, and every
existing health signal (GAME_UPDATE, GAME_POWER start/restart) only ever confirmed the
container/systemd-service OBJECT existed — never that the game process actually bound its port — so
this went undetected.

**Research, not a guess.** Checked itzg/docker-minecraft-server's own docs
(`docs/versions/java.md`) for whether the image auto-selects the right JDK from the requested
`VERSION` — it explicitly does not: tags are static per Java version, and the docs point at the same
Minecraft-wiki table used below rather than doing the mapping themselves. `latest`/`stable` DO
auto-track whichever Java the newest release needs (java25 today), but floating with whatever Mojang
ships next is the same footgun already fixed once for the `VERSION` field itself (the 2026-09-06
Cobblemon incident, above) — an unannounced future Java bump on those tags could just as easily break
an old pinned-version modded server. Went with a pinned, versioned cutover table instead — the real
Mojang cutovers (minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorials/Update_Java, confirmed live 2026-09-20):

| Minecraft version | Minimum Java |
|---|---|
| 26.1 and newer | 25 |
| 1.20.5 – 1.21.11 | 21 |
| 1.18 – 1.20.4 | 17 |
| 1.17 – 1.17.1 | 16 |
| 1.0 – 1.16.5 | 8 |

All five `itzg/minecraft-server:javaN` tags were verified to genuinely exist against Docker Hub's own
registry API (HTTP 200 on each of java25/java21/java17/java16/java8) before being used anywhere —
never assumed.

**Implementation** (`lib/game-config.ts`: `MINECRAFT_JAVA_CUTOVERS`, `requiredJavaMajorForMinecraftVersion`,
`minecraftImageForVersion`, `javaMajorOfMinecraftImage`):

- **Provision time** (`worker/game-variant.ts`'s new `applyMinecraftJavaImage`, wired into
  `worker/index.ts`'s `buildCloudInit`): rewrites the catalog's image tag to whatever Java the
  customer's checkout-time `VERSION` actually needs. Falls back to the schema's own default
  (1.21.1 → java21) when `gameConfig` carries no VERSION, so an order that never touches the field
  sees no behavior change.
- **Settings-time version change** (`worker/game-config.ts`'s `applyMinecraft`): now computes the
  required Java major for the target VERSION and compares it against the currently-running image's
  own tag (`javaMajorOfMinecraftImage`). Recreates the container on a genuine shortfall
  (`imageInsufficient`: current Java major is null/unknown or below what's required) — **never** for
  a server already running Java equal to or above what its version needs. This is deliberate: it is
  what makes the fix additive/corrective rather than a blanket image bump — an existing java21 server
  on an old, already-working version is left untouched.
- Kept all four new-format versions (26.2/26.1.2/26.1.1/26.1) in `MINECRAFT_RELEASE_VERSIONS` — the
  java25 tag is real and satisfies all of them, so there was no need to pull any of them from the
  picker.

**Health-check gap fixed alongside it** (`worker/provision-health.ts`, `worker/game-control.ts`):
`gamePower` (GAME_POWER start/restart) used to notify success once `systemctl`'s exit code was 0 and
an end marker was seen, without ever checking whether the resulting state was actually `active` — a
`Restart=always` unit around a crash-looping container reports "active" between crashes just as
readily as a healthy server does. Now: (1) a non-`stop` action whose resulting state isn't `active`
is a reported failure, and (2) once `active`, a short real port-bound check
(`checkGamePortOpen` + `gamePortBoundInGuest`, the same in-guest positive-confirmation path PROVISION
already used) confirms the game process itself bound its port before declaring success — families
with no `GAME_PORT` entry, or a NAT server whose port isn't forwarded, skip this silently rather than
block. `gamePortBoundInGuest` was moved from a private function in `worker/index.ts` into the
side-effect-free `worker/provision-health.ts` so `worker/game-control.ts` could reuse it directly
(importing `worker/index.ts` elsewhere is unsafe — it runs a top-level job-polling `main()` loop).
